text:
alex: Quick question — we're finalizing envelope encryption design for multi-cloud. want to lock down DEK/KEK caching and rotation strategy before the RBAC changes land. thoughts?

maria: High level: use per-tenant DEKs (short TTL) + KEK in KMS per-region. minimize KMS calls by caching plaintext DEKs in memory with short TTL and evict on rotation. keep ciphertext DEK in DB.

jamal: Agree on per-tenant DEKs. Two tradeoffs to call out: memory-caching plaintext DEKs reduces KMS ops but raises exposure (process memory). caching only ciphertext DEKs forces decrypt per request -> heavy KMS rate usage.

olga: We should prefer caching plaintext DEKs in a sealed in-process cache and rotate frequently. Also add a configurable threshold: if decrypt ops > X/s, spawn a local decrypt worker pool to amortize unwrapping and avoid thundering herds.

alex: Good. For cloud differences: AWS KMS GenerateDataKey/GCP CryptoKey versions/ Azure wrapKey semantics — any gotchas?

maria: AWS: use GenerateDataKey without exposing KEK to code. returns {Plaintext, CiphertextBlob}. store CiphertextBlob, cache Plaintext in memory. Watch CloudTrail for Decrypt/GenerateDataKey events. Rate limits: ~1000 TPS per key (varies). GCP: similar ReEncrypt pattern, but key versioning differs; use key version id in envelope header. Azure: wrapKey/unwrap can be slower; watch soft quotas.

jamal: Also: use a standardized envelope metadata header attached to blobs: something like `v=1;prov=aws;key=arn:...;ver=3;alg=AES-256-GCM;iv=...` so any runtime can rewrap or fall back across clouds.

olga: Example header we use in prototype: `{"v":"1","provider":"aws","key_id":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/abc","key_version":"3","enc":"AES-GCM-256"}`. keep it compact in binary format for perf.

alex: Audit logging + RBAC: what events do we need?

maria: Mandatory: all GenerateDataKey/Decrypt/Encrypt/WrapKey/UnwrapKey calls, with principal, request-id, purpose tag, and blob-id. Ship KMS logs to our central SIEM and correlate with app audit events. RBAC: service account roles split: `kms:encrypt` for wrap-only services, `kms:decrypt` for workers that actually need plaintext. grant decrypt narrowly.

jamal: For rotation: prefer re-wrap-on-read (lazy rewrap) for large datasets, plus background rewrap job for cold data. When rotating KEK, keep old key version for decryption until we successfully rewrap all ciphertexts.

olga: Incident scenario: if a KEK is suspected compromised -> steps: 1) disable key version in KMS (prevents new unwraps if supported), 2) spin new KEK, 3) rewrap DEK ciphertexts using new KEK (background), 4) rotate cached plaintext DEKs immediately by fetching new GenerateDataKey or rewrap and replace in memory, 5) audit and notify customers. Document action timeline and pre-authorized playbook.

alex: Good. How about KMS call frequency and throttling mitigation?

maria: Techniques: local plaintext DEK cache with TTL (e.g., 5m default), sharded in-process caches keyed by tenant, circuit-breaker when KMS error rates spike, exponential backoff. Pre-warm caches for hot tenants. Use batching for decrypt operations where possible (worker unwrapping 50 items in one burst).

jamal: Also consider caching plaintext DEKs in a small HSM-backed process (if available) to reduce process memory footprint and make memory scraping harder. For private deployments, customers may have HSM/HV support.

olga: Vulnerability triage notes: if a host with cached plaintext DEKs is compromised, scope is limited to tenants whose DEKs were cached on that host. That's why per-tenant DEKs are crucial. Also rotate DEKs on suspected compromise and force rewrap.

alex: Any RBAC or audit policy changes we should submit with this design?

maria: Submit PR to: 1) split `kms:decrypt` role from general infra role, 2) require `purpose` tag on all GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls, 3) add alert when Decrypts spikes > 3x baseline for a key, 4) retention policy for KMS audit logs >= 1 year for enterprise customers.

olga: Add requirement: key access is only allowed from specific CIDR ranges for private deployments and require MFA or approved service principals for rotation operations.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling RBAC change scheduled in eng-iam on 1803550000 UTC. Will apply `kms-decrypt` separation in staging first.

alex: Final checklist for docs/engineers: - envelope format spec - cache implementation guide (TTL, eviction, secure memory) - rotation playbook (immediate+background rewrap) - RBAC PR and SIEM pipeline for KMS logs - incident response runbook. I'll draft the spec today and share.

maria: SGTM. If you want I can add sample code for GenerateDataKey + store ciphertext & cache plaintext.

jamal: Please include metrics to track: KMS calls/sec per key, cache hit rate, decrypt latency percentiles, and incidents triggered.

olga: I'll add the rewrap worker design and a simulation script to estimate KMS ops for rewrap.

alex: Thanks — will post draft link here when ready. :thumbsup:
